entities.summary: James McHenry was an Scots-Irish American military surgeon, statesman, and a Founding Father of the United States. McHenry was a signer of the United States Constitution from Maryland, initiated the recommendation for Congress to form the Navy, and was the eponym of Fort McHenry. He represented Maryland in the Continental Congress. He was a delegate to the Maryland State Convention of 1788, to vote whether Maryland should ratify the proposed Constitution of the United States. He served as United States Secretary of War from 1796 to 1800, bridging the administrations of George Washington and John Adams.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a Founding Father and statesman, McHenry played a crucial role in shaping the United States Constitution and its ratification process. His recommendation for Congress to form the Navy also laid the groundwork for the country's future naval power.
